metadata.description: Post-core feature backlog for PhotoBlaze. These ship AFTER the core viewer is stable (roadmap Phases 0-3: window, decode-to-fit, prefetch ring, hold-to-fly). Every task obeys the prime directive (faster or perf-neutral) and the project's TDD rules: pure logic isolated and unit-tested, GPU work behind the Renderer seam, golden-image tests for visuals. Shared infrastructure is factored out so it is built once: a per-photo ViewTransform (rotation + zoom + scaling mode), a translucent HUD/overlay layer, and a central configurable action/keymap.

tasks.title: Windows: single-instance window reuse + Explorer multi-select as one playlist
tasks.description: Make Windows match the macOS open idiom (LaunchServices already gives the Mac one instance + one openURLs batch). Today each Explorer double-click/Open spawns a FULL new process (decode pool + resident VRAM ring each; settings.toml write races), and multi-select Open invokes one process per file (Explorer blocks >15 selections by default — MultipleInvokePromptMinimum — so the blast radius is capped at ~15 processes, but that is still bad). Plan: (a) accept multiple CLI path args -> classify_inputs (the Vec<PathBuf> -> LaunchInput::Files machinery already serves drag-drop/picker); (b) MultiSelectModel=Player on the ProgID (MSI AppRegistration component + the HKCU self-registration fallback in default_app.rs) so a multi-select arrives as ONE invocation; (c) single-instance: named mutex, loser forwards its paths via WM_COPYDATA to the running instance (-> open_paths -> open_plan) and exits, winner comes to front (AllowSetForegroundWindow) — this also merges the multiple invocations Explorer emits when a huge selection overflows the ~32K command line. Compare-two-photos is NOT this task: thats #43 (or a future explicit File > New Window command, which the mutex design must not preclude — e.g. a --new-window flag bypass). MSIX/Store evaluation moved out to decisions.md (revisit only if monetizing). Windows machine required.
tasks.details: Milestone C (ADR-018). Set-default: a button/hotkey opens ms-settings:defaultapps (or the Default Programs UI), since Windows forbids silent default seizure. Single-instance (optional): forward a newly-opened path to the running window (named pipe / mutex) instead of spawning a second window - nicer for double-click bursts; defer if it complicates the hot path. A modern Win11 inline folder verb would need an IExplorerCommand COM handler - only pursue if the 'Show more options' legacy verb from Task 13 feels inadequate. MSIX/Store: revisit only when charging money - it buys discovery + MS-managed signing/updates but costs the cheap folder verb and adds container friction.
tasks.testStrategy: Manual: 'Set as default' opens the right Settings page; a second launch with single-instance adopts the new photo in the existing window. MSIX evaluation deferred.

tasks.title: Spike: higher-quality HEIC preview than the 320x240 thumbnail
tasks.description: Owner hunch (likely an easy quality lever): find a better embedded preview than WIC's 320x240 GetThumbnail. From the HEIF dump, an iPhone HEIC has only the 320x240 thumb (item 50) + the full 48-tile grid + a 2016x1512 `auxl/auxC` aux (item 51) believed to be the HDR gain map. Verify item 51 (gain map vs usable preview), and check non-iPhone/Sony HEICs (DSC*.heic) for a true mid-res single-hvc1 preview. If a usable mid-res image exists, decode IT for the preview: ~6x sharper, one fast decode (no grid). Needs libheif or a HEIF item extractor.

(2) Fill mode decodes full-res (decode_fit returns None for Fill+Original; give Fill a cover-to-screen target). (3) Decode-pool byte budget is a soft cap (reserve-before-decode; largely moot now). (4) DecodeKind::{Preview,Full} in the pool key (defensive). (5) Sync load paths (startup/resize/mode) bypass preview-first -> ~250ms HEIC freeze. (6) No unit/property tests for the tier state machine (extract pure bits).

tasks.title: Clipboard affordances on the EXIF info panel (copy all / copy one field)
tasks.description: UNCOOKED IDEA (owner, 2026-06-28) - needs design before building. On the Shift+I full-EXIF overlay, add a small clipboard icon in the panel's corner that copies the whole info block as text, and let clicking an individual field copy just that one value. Could be genuinely useful for grabbing a camera/lens/exposure string or a file path without retyping. Capturing it as a low-priority backlog item, not a committed design.
tasks.details: EXPLORATORY - the interaction model is the open question, because the info/EXIF overlay is NOT egui. It's a software-composited RGBA8 pill rasterized in pb-app/src/hud.rs (render_table) and drawn as a single alpha-blended GPU quad via Renderer::set_overlay (one texture, rebuilt only on change, off the photo hot path). So unlike the Settings/About dialogs there are no interactive widgets to hang a click handler on - 'click a field to copy it' needs explicit HIT-TESTING: map the cursor position (minus the overlay's corner margin + the panel's row layout from render_table) back to a specific Row, then copy that row's value. That row geometry currently lives only inside the rasterizer, so it would need to expose per-row rects (or a click-to-row helper) for the event loop to test against. The whole-panel 'copy all' is the easy half: assemble the same Vec<Row> the panel renders (App::exif_rows) into text and write it. OPEN QUESTIONS to resolve first: (a) is text-on-an-overlay click-to-copy worth the hit-testing machinery, or should the full-EXIF view become a real interactive surface (egui) instead, which would make per-field copy/selection trivial but is a bigger change and pulls EXIF into the chrome stack; (b) discoverability + affordance - a static clipboard glyph in the corner implies 'copy all', but 'click any row to copy that row' is invisible without a hover highlight (which the static-bitmap overlay can't currently show without a rebuild per mouse-move); (c) feedback - reuse the existing toast ('Copied') so the user knows it worked. REUSE: clipboard text I/O can ride the same arboard dep added for image copy (#27, pb-app/src/clipboard.rs - currently set_image; add a set_text path); the corner icon would follow the HUD Font Awesome solid workflow (hud.rs icon compositing, FA solid per CLAUDE.md); exif_rows already builds the field list. Decide the interaction model (overlay hit-test vs. promote EXIF to egui) before committing to an implementation.
tasks.testStrategy: Pure: a unit test for 'rows -> clipboard text' (formatting, label:value lines, ordering) and, if the overlay hit-test route is taken, a pure cursor-position -> row-index mapping test (mirrors the render_table layout; off-panel / between-rows returns None). Manual: Shift+I, click the corner icon and paste the whole block elsewhere; click a single field and paste just that value; confirm the 'Copied' toast fires and that copying never writes anything to disk (privacy #2 - clipboard is a user-initiated action, not a viewing trace).

tasks.title: Flicker compare mode: pin (Shift+Y) + instant A/B toggle (Y)
tasks.description: Owner-approved 2026-07-03 — full design + implementation order in .taskmaster/docs/compare-mode-plan.md. Y pins the current photo, then flips instantly between the pin and wherever you are (full-screen flicker comparison — perceptually better than side-by-side for culling, and a keypress-is-a-rebind cheap in this engine). Shift+Y moves/clears the pin. Zoom/pan carries across same-dimension flips (the 100%-crop sharpness workflow). Pin is RAM-only (privacy ADR-018), survives playlist rebuilds by name, unpins on delete. The pinned texture is exempt from ring eviction so the flip never decodes. Split view demoted to an optional phase 2 reusing the same pin state; a future squoosh-style export preview can ride the same toggle seam. IMPLEMENTED 2026-07-03: all five build subtasks landed in one session, workspace green (150+ tests incl. 7 new compare semantics tests + 2 playlist jump_to tests), clippy -D warnings, fmt, swift host builds. Live-smoked on the corpus: pin 1/15, browse, Y flips 1<->3 then 1<->4 (return point follows) — trace-verified.

tasks.title: AI image description (on-device / local models only)
tasks.description: DETAILED PLAN: .taskmaster/docs/ai-descriptions-plan.md (2026-07-03). Describe the current image with a vision model. Trigger: `D` (rebindable; menu + context menu), result overlaid where the detailed info panel goes; optional auto-describe when the user PARKS on an image >500 ms (EAGER_PREP_DELAY pattern) — cancelled on advance (generation counter), results cached RAM-only per image (meta_cache pattern), dropped on exit. Auto mode is an opt-in toggle: fine by construction on the Apple on-device backend, but a configured endpoint could be remote, and passive sends must be a deliberate choice. Two backends behind one core-owned seam/policy: (1) macOS 27+ Foundation Models framework (on-device, image input, ships with the OS); (2) an OpenAI-compatible local endpoint (LM Studio / llama.cpp / Ollama — Qwen3-VL-8B or 27B-class on an RTX 5090) for Windows and power users. One-shot v1 (streaming later if slow; expected 1–5 s). Prompt built in core so both backends match: salient EXIF (capture time, camera/lens, raw GPS coords — offline reverse-geocoder is a LATER upgrade), filename + parent folder; all context framed as UNVERIFIED (trust-the-pixels instruction — hallucination guard) with epoch-default junk dates filtered out. Custom prompt template = advanced, settings.toml-only in v1 ({filename}/{folder}/{datetime}/{location}/{camera} placeholders). Optional TTS via CoreEffect::Speak — AVSpeechSynthesizer / Windows.Media.SpeechSynthesis, offline system voices, speech stops on navigation. New 'AI Descriptions' settings section (own tab on macOS): backend picker (Auto/Apple/Local), endpoint URL + model, auto-describe toggle, speak-aloud toggle. Privacy (ADR-018): never cloud, RAM-only, no sidecars/caches on disk; the endpoint URL + toggles are the only persisted config. v1 scope: on-disk stills (archive entries punted like Delete). Prerequisite: pb-hud font-fallback cascade — model output is arbitrary, possibly non-Latin prose. Additions from final discussion: 'Speak descriptions' is ALSO a menu toggle (Image menu, Mute-Live-Photo-Audio pattern, MenuState checkbox); the AI Descriptions settings section carries a short privacy blurb (custom endpoint = your images upload to that URL, incl. auto-describe — keep it local/trusted; online services may retain/train on images).

tasks.title: Copy Text from Image / Show Text (on-device OCR + QR codes)
tasks.description: DETAILED PLAN: .taskmaster/docs/ai-descriptions-plan.md (OCR section, 2026-07-03). Tier 1 only: on-demand OCR of the current image — 'Copy Text from Image' in the Edit/context menus (clipboard + toast) and `T` to show recognized text in a HUD panel. Engines are OS-built-in and fully on-device: macOS Vision RecognizeTextRequest (NO macOS 27 dependency — available on the current floor; Swift-side via the same delegate/FFI shape as the FM describe backend) and Windows.Media.Ocr via the windows crate (worker thread, downscaled input ≤ OcrEngine.MaxImageDimension, language packs required). Shares task #44's state machine (busy/generation-cancel/RAM-only cache) and the ClipboardPayload::Text seam. Tier 2 (VisionKit Live Text overlay) and Tier 3 (cross-platform selection UI) deliberately punted — recorded in the plan doc. GARNISH: QR/barcode payloads via a pure-Rust decoder (rxing or rqrr) on BOTH platforms (Windows has no OS barcode API; one shared backend, no FFI, testable with generated QR PNGs). ⚠ Decode from FULL-RES RGBA, not the OCR downscale (pixels-per-module). Payloads list above the text in the T panel and ride the copy command — no new key/menu item.

tasks.title: Light mode support for the HUD (appearance preference: System/Light/Dark)
tasks.description: The HUD rasterizer (pb-hud/src/hud.rs) currently hardcodes always-white text ([255,255,255]) with a black shadow/outline (tokens::TEXT/TEXT_DIM/SHADOW, hud.rs ~30-38) and a translucent-black panel background (tokens::BG) - there is no color/theme parameter threaded through render_table/render_centered/render_panel today, only background alpha is parameterized. Add a user-facing Appearance preference (System/Light/Dark, defaulting to System = current dark-on-black look unchanged) that flips the HUD to black text with a white shadow/halo and a light translucent panel background when resolved-light. Reuse the existing OS theme detection already used for the egui dialog window (winit's Window::theme() in pb-app/src/dialog.rs:404, dark_ui = window.theme() != Some(Theme::Light)) rather than hand-rolling a new registry/NSAppearance check - it already covers Windows (AppsUseLightTheme/DWM) and macOS (NSApp.effectiveAppearance) portably. Settings storage follows the existing ScaleModePref/StartupMode enum pattern in pb-app-core/src/settings.rs (Copy/Default/Serialize/Deserialize, #[serde(rename_all = "lowercase")], #[default] variant, TOML-persisted, round-trip tested).
